name: sol_ll_3
description: Low-level call to address without checking it has deployed code
question: The source file in `source` performs a low-level call, staticcall, or delegatecall to an address without verifying that the target address contains deployed code, such that a call to an empty or non-existent address silently returns success, potentially causing the calling logic to incorrectly assume the operation succeeded; this excludes cases where the target is a known trusted contract address that is guaranteed to have code, or where the return value handling does not rely on call success alone.
criteria: A function makes a low-level call() to a user-supplied or configurable address and treats the call as successful based only on the boolean success return value, without checking address.code.length > 0 or extcodesize before the call
A function performs a delegatecall to an address parameter without first verifying the target has deployed code, allowing a call to an empty address to appear successful
A function performs a staticcall to an address to read data without checking that the address has code, treating an empty return as valid data instead of reverting
A token transfer or external interaction pattern manually implements call() to send funds or invoke a function on an address without any code-existence check before or after the call
